candidate_relations.reason: Systemic lupus erythematosus is the lupus family but asserts idiopathic SLE rather than isoniazid/RIPE-induced lupus.
Tuberculous pleurisy was the working explanation for the lymphocyte-rich effusion but conflicts with repeatedly negative cultures, negative QuantiFERON, and non-granulomatous biopsies.
Sjögren syndrome is a different autoimmune disease not supported as the cause of recurrent drug-associated pleural effusions.
Rheumatoid arthritis is a different autoimmune disease and does not match this RIPE-associated serosal process.
Paradoxical tuberculous effusion was the prior clinical attribution and is incompatible with the requested drug-induced lupus object.
Waldenström macroglobulinemia is a different hematologic cause of effusions and is not indicated.
Chylothorax is a different effusion type; the fluid is an exudative lymphocytic effusion, not described as chyle.
Sarcoidosis is a different granulomatous disease; pleural biopsies lacked granulomas.
Lymphoma is a different neoplastic cause of recurrent effusion and cytology/biopsies were not lymphomatous.
Tuberculosis is the disease for which RIPE was started, not the final drug-induced lupus diagnosis causing recurrent culture-negative effusions.
Idiopathic pleuritis names the serositis without the required drug-induced lupus etiology.
Pleural disease is a compatible parent finding of recurrent effusion but lacks the drug-induced lupus diagnosis.
Castleman disease is a different lymphoproliferative entity not supported by the record.
Drug-induced lupus erythematosus is an alias of the reference drug-induced lupus after prolonged RIPE with ANA-positive recurrent lymphocytic effusions.

case_quality_flags: Serum ANA is only 1:160 speckled and antihistone antibody is negative, which is atypical for classic drug-induced lupus, but the reference remains DIL after RIPE.
